attempts.bug_summary: When both a palette image and background color are supplied, palette generation uses the input image instead of the supplied palette image. This causes the background setting to alter which image provides the indexed color model, despite the palette image taking precedence during conversion.

The row raster is clipped using the destination-band selection instead of the source-band selection. This produces incorrect channel mapping or failures when source and destination band arrays differ.

The fallback path for streams without DC Huffman tables is made dependent on the AC table selector instead of the DC selector. When the two selectors differ, this can select the wrong Huffman tables or trigger an exception while decoding.

attempts.bug_summary: When initializing the predictor, the decoder combines the scan's spectral selection with its point-transform value. For scans that use both a non-default spectral selection and a point transform, this starts prediction from the wrong midpoint and causes the decoded component values to diverge.

The truecolor read path applies vertical subsampling where horizontal subsampling is required and passes the two subsampling factors in reversed order. Images read with unequal source X and Y subsampling therefore produce incorrectly sampled pixel data while symmetric subsampling remains unaffected.

attempts.bug_summary: When reading planar multi-channel images, the source row is clipped using the destination-band selection rather than the requested source-band selection. Reads that combine distinct source-band and destination-band mappings therefore copy different channels than requested, while default band settings remain unaffected.

When source-region selection and subsampling are used together, the code derives the subsampling offsets from the region's absolute origin. This causes non-aligned regions to skip initial pixels and produce different image dimensions or content than the requested region with zero read offsets.

The method preserves the existing TIFF interpretation and color-model selection paths, but alpha premultiplication is derived from the trailing extra-sample entry rather than the entry that establishes alpha semantics. This affects images containing alpha together with additional unspecified extra samples.

The combined predictor path reuses the top pixel as the final averaging input and no longer incorporates the top-right pixel into the result. This affects pixels using the four-neighbor average predictor, particularly where the top-right value differs from the other neighbors.

For the full clamp-add-subtract predictor, the top-left and top neighbor inputs are supplied in the wrong roles. This changes the reconstructed pixel only for CLAMP_ADD_SUB_FULL selections where those neighboring values produce different clamped results.

Macroblock-boundary filtering for the chroma planes uses the subblock edge limit instead of the macroblock edge limit. This affects both left and top neighboring macroblock edges while leaving inner subblock filtering unchanged.

When sharpness adjustment is enabled, the interior limit is capped using the loop-filter level rather than the sharpness level. This changes filtering for combinations of high filter levels and nonzero sharpness, especially when the sharpness cap would otherwise preserve a larger interior limit.

The method remains valid and preserves all existing prediction modes and surrounding behavior. A coordinated indexing change in the TM prediction path causes the vertical boundary samples to be selected from the current horizontal subblock index rather than the corresponding neighboring column.
